transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-10-07 15:30 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Head of AI, Harborview), Ethan Cole (Security Architect, Harborview), Maria Lopez (DevOps, Harborview)

Summary: quick scoping for a security-focused pilot evaluating Redwood Private/Dedicated options. Discussed SOC 2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, VPC connectivity, workload sizing and performance benchmarks, and timelines for a 6-week pilot.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we should have about 45 minutes, will do quick intros then dive into security and the pilot scope.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, Priya here, leading ML at Harborview, we've been exploring LLM features for internal clinical summarization, privacy is obviously the top concern.
[00:20] Ethan: Ethan, security architect, want to make sure auditability, key management and SSO are covered.
[00:27] Marco: Marco Ruiz, SE on the Redwood side, I'll handle benchmarks and deployment questions.
[00:33] Maria: Maria, DevOps, I'll be coordinating networking and infraâ€”VPC, peering, etc.
[00:40] Lena: Great. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, talk workload sizing and benchmarks, then deep dive security/compliance items and next steps.

[02:05] Priya: For success criteria we have three main pillars: accuracy of the summaries (measured by a small eval set), latency p95 under 800ms for interactive use, and data handling requirementsâ€”no PHI left unencrypted and audit logs retained for 1 year.
[02:28] Lena: That's helpful. For latency target, are you aiming for hosted API or private/dedicated?
[02:35] Priya: Ideally Private in our VPC but if dedicated in a Redwood-managed environment meets the audit we can consider that. Main thing is we need SSO and RBAC to map to our roles.

[04:10] Marco: On sizing, can you share expected QPS and average token sizes? That drives GPU selection and whether batching is feasible.
[04:18] Priya: Roughly 20 concurrent users initially, about 10 reqs/s steady during peak, average prompt 400 tokens, average generation 600 tokens so about 1k tokens per request.
[04:35] Marco: So 10 reqs/sec * 1k tokens => 10k tokens/sec, for a pilot we'll likely provision a small dedicated pool, and run benchmarks at 5, 10, 20 users to validate.
[04:49] Maria: What's our expected concurrency pattern? Bursty or steady?
[04:52] Priya: More bursty during morning rounds, peaks up to 30 reqs/s for short periods.

[06:20] Marco: For benchmarks we'll run an end-to-end test: your prompt sets, 95th percentile latency, token throughput, and failure/retry behavior. We can run both hosted and private variants; for security pilot it's better to test within your VPC or with dedicated instances.

[08:00] Ethan: On security, SOC 2 and ISO are table stakes. We need attestation docs, syslogs and audit logs, SSO via SAML or OIDC, RBAC integration with our IDP, and KMS integration for key control. Also retention policies and the ability to export logs for audits.
[08:23] Lena: We can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificates; I'll attach them. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM for Private or Dedicated; for hosted we have keys but can discuss Bring-Your-Own-Key for Dedicated.
[08:42] Ethan: Good. For audit logs we need field-level details: who called the API, model used, prompt hash, timestamp, IP, and response status. Can you capture prompt hashes rather than raw prompts if needed?
[09:04] Marco: Yes, we can log prompt hashes and full prompt if retention policy allows; we have configurable log capture levels. We also have per-token cost and latency breakdowns in Console.

[11:20] Maria: Network: do you support VPC peering or private link? We need traffic to stay within our network.
[11:30] Marco: For Private deployments we support VPC peering and direct on-prem connectors. For Dedicated we can set up VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on region.
[11:40] Maria: And do you support IP allowlists and SAML assertion-based role mapping?
[11:45] Marco: Yes, IP allowlists and SAML; RBAC can sync groups from your IdP.

[13:10] Priya: On data residencyâ€”we need logs stored in our region (US-East) and encryption at rest.
[13:18] Lena: We have region controls for Private and Dedicated; hosted has region options too but for strict residency Private is recommended.

[15:00] Ethan: A few more nitty-gritty items: Do you provide immutable audit logs for compliance? Can logs be exported to our SIEM (e.g., Splunk)?
[15:12] Marco: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM via Kafka or S3 export; immutability we can support via write-once S3 and retention policies.
[15:25] Ethan: Great. Also will the pilot include a handshake for SAML metadata and cert rotation processes?
[15:33] Lena: Yes we'll share SAML metadata and a runbook for cert rotation.

[17:05] Priya: Regarding success criteria for qualityâ€”we'll run an eval of 500 clinical notes and expect the extractive summary F1 to be >= 0.78 compared to our gold set. That's part of acceptance.
[17:22] Marco: We'll run the eval on your eval set during the benchmark and provide quality regressions monitoring. We can also enable automatic rollback to a previous model if quality drops.

[19:00] Maria: How long to spin up a Private environment for pilot?
[19:05] Marco: If it's a VPC-based private deployment and you provide network details, initial provisioning is 3-5 business days for a small pilot; Dedicated reserved capacity takes longer because of commit timelines.
[19:18] Maria: And costsâ€”do you have a pilot pricing model?
[19:22] Lena: We typically provide a 6-week pilot with a fixed config and usage cap; we'll share pricing in the SOW. For tight security pilots we often recommend Dedicated with customer-managed keys.

[21:40] Ethan: For encryption, do you redact PHI before logging or can you apply prompt hashing on the fly?
[21:50] Marco: We can configure to only store prompt hashes in logs; additionally you can set up a preprocessor to redact PHI client-side before sending.

[23:10] Priya: Timeline: We want pilot to start by 2026-10-25 if possible, run 6 weeks, and deliver final decision by mid-December.
[23:22] Lena: That timeline is doable: next week we'll send docs, week of Oct 18 we plan the benchmark run, aim to start deployment the week of Oct 25.

[25:00] Marco: Benchmark plan: 1) deploy small private stack in your VPC, 2) run 30-minute smoke, 3) run 1-hour throughput test at 10 and 30 req/s with your prompt set, 4) run quality eval on 500 notes. We'll share results and a post-mortem.

[27:30] Ethan: Also want to ensure SIEM exports, rotation policies, and a runbook for incident response are available.
[27:40] Lena: We'll attach incident response playbook and contact list for the pilot.

[30:00] Priya: One blocker: legal needs insurance certificate and Data Processing Addendum with standard clauses for health dataâ€”are you able to provide those?
[30:12] Lena: Yes, we have a DPA and can provide proof of cyber insurance; legal team will follow up.

[33:00] Maria: For role mapping, we want RBAC roles mapped to our groups: clinician, admin, auditor. Can you enforce least privilege on model access?
[33:12] Marco: Yes RBAC supports custom roles and policy enforcement; auditors can be given read-only access to logs and audit trails.

[35:00] Priya: Any limitations around model quantization or specific open models we must avoid for compliance?
[35:08] Marco: From a compliance perspective, it's about where the model inference runs and data handling. We can avoid uploads to third-party model stores and pin to vetted open weights; we also have Redwood-verified profiles indicating which quantizations we recommend.

[37:40] Ethan: For the benchmark, please log per-request metadata keys we specified: user_id, request_id, model_id, prompt_hash, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, status_code.
[37:55] Marco: Noted, we'll include those fields in the audit log schema and share the mapping.

[40:10] Lena: Let's recap next steps: we'll send SOC 2/ISO docs, DPA, SAML integration guide, pilot SOW and pricing; Marco will share benchmark plan and we schedule the run week of Oct 18; Priya will provide prompt/eval sets.
[40:30] Priya: Sounds good. We'll also confirm network contacts and provide required IDs for SAML.

[42:00] Lena: Any other risks or blockers?
[42:05] Ethan: No blockers beyond legal review and ensuring we can get the logs exported to our SIEM.
[42:12] Maria: We need to validate VPC peering during test.

[44:00] Lena: OK thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the attachments; next call to review benchmark results tentatively Nov 1.
[44:12] Marco: Thanks, we'll get the plan out by Friday.
[44:20] Priya: Thanks all.
